Price book

Every estimate line prices from here: material per unit for Good, Better and Best, crew labor hours per unit, what a sub charges per unit for work A&H normally subs out, and waste. The senior estimator owns these numbers. Lines marked Market allowance are priced from Las Vegas market ranges until A&H's own numbers replace them: enter what the work really took in Jobs → Job file → Allowance check, then tap "Use job average" here.

Backup and restore

A full copy of the app's records (estimates, jobs, invoices, homes, accounts, work orders, campaigns, daily logs, change order requests, settings and price book, plus customers and the team list if you can see them) in one file you keep. The same file restores into this app or into the company server copy of the app. Photos stay where they are; the file lists them.

Settings

How it works

The customer gets a price within 24 hours of the visit. Each role sees its own queue.

  1. Measure tech starts a visit, picks the types of work, and goes step by step through measurements, photos, condition checks, who does the work, and the customer's choice for each one, and records the customer's Good / Better / Best choice. Submit unlocks only when nothing is missing. The 24-hour clock starts.
  2. The app turns measurements into quantities, adds waste, and prices every line from the price book.
  3. Estimator checks the draft against the photos, adds anything the price book doesn't cover, checks the margin, and sends it for approval.
  4. Roles come from your sign-in. The owner or an Editor lists the team under Price book → Team and roles and ticks each person's roles. "Working as" only offers your roles, and only a Senior estimator can approve, except that an Estimator can approve and send an estimate under $5,000 that is at the target margin.
  5. Customer ready to sign at the visit? The tech taps "Customer is ready: get a quick OK". The estimate is priced from the price book and the senior estimator sees "Customer waiting" at the top of their Estimates screen. Once they approve, the customer reviews the proposal on the tech's phone, types their name, signs with a finger and accepts. The estimate becomes Won with a job number, and the signed proposal (with the right-to-cancel notice) can be printed or emailed.
  6. Senior estimator approves, or returns it with notes. Approved estimates are marked sent and follow-ups begin.
  7. Money picks up once the customer signs: create invoices from the payment schedule, a work order, or a Home Depot program or steel job, or record invoices made in another system. Record each payment as it comes in, and the Money tab shows open estimates, what is ready to bill, open and overdue invoices, and what was collected.
  8. Customers are entered once by the office and fill in the proposal, home profile and invoices. Measure techs and estimators see the customer on their estimate but can't change it: corrections and new customers they send wait in the Customers tab until someone with Editor access approves them. Customer details stay out of reports and spreadsheet copies.
  9. Numbers follow your trackers. Each new estimate gets a lead # (261024-054 = lead 54 of the year, taken Oct 24). When a job is won, or a work order or program job is created, it gets a job # (26-40-015 = 2026, Remodels, job 15). Each channel counts separately, both counts start over every January 1, and the job # rides along on every invoice.
  10. Jobs shows every job from proposal to paid. Money → Monthly and quarterly reports gives any month, quarter or year, downloadable as a spreadsheet or printable as a PDF. Money → Collections lists everything owed, oldest first, with a follow-up log.
  11. Baseline price comes straight from the measurements and the customer's choices: every price-book line has a customer price per sq ft, lin ft or each (Price book shows it). If the site makes the job harder or easier than normal, the tech or estimator adds an adjustment with a note (second floor, occupied home, out of level and so on). The senior estimator sees every adjustment before approving, and the customer sees only the final price.
  12. Schedule lists the week's visits, walkthroughs, inspections and deliveries by day, with who goes and the address (tap it for directions). "Add to my calendar" puts an appointment on your phone with a 1-hour reminder, and "Text customer" opens a confirmation text. Every sent estimate gets follow-ups on day 3, 7 and 14, then every 2 weeks, until it is marked Won or Lost; the Estimates screen shows what is due today.
  13. Time: clock in on a job and cost code, take breaks, switch jobs and clock out. Assigned crew see their jobs first. Forgotten time is added by hand with a reason; every fix is kept with who and why. Submit the week; the office approves it. People with payroll access also see a Payroll box for the pay period (every other week by default) with regular, overtime and double time hours and dollars, salary, labor burden and total cost, and can export it. Job costs and reports then use each person's real pay instead of the loaded rate.
  14. Reports (Time → Labor and job cost reports, office only) group hours, labor cost and job costs by cost code, job, job type, line of business, state, person, week or month, with a second level, filters, a spreadsheet download and print.
  15. Job file (Jobs → Job file) holds the crew, the daily log, the punch list with customer sign-off, material orders with late flags, job costs against the estimate (labor from the time clock at the loaded rate, materials, subs and lien waivers) and warranty calls, checked against the 1-year workmanship warranty.
  16. Subs & vendors keeps each sub's W-9, insurance and license dates and signed agreement; missing or expired papers show in red.
  17. Daily log: on every won job (Jobs → Daily log), everyone who clocks in files one entry for the day with the cost code, work done, progress, photos tagged Before, During or After, delays, inspections and safety. The weather fills in from the job location. Once submitted, an entry cannot be changed; later fixes are dated notes. Change order requests from the field go to the estimator. The office can check a BusyBusy time export against who filed a log.
  18. Closeout packet: when a job is finished, open it from the job board or the estimate. It lists the products installed (from the estimate, plus anything added), the care pages for those trades and the 1-year workmanship warranty. Print it for the final walkthrough, have the customer sign, then email the PDF. Edit the care pages and warranty wording in Price book → Settings.
  19. Allowance prices: price-book lines without an A&H cost yet are priced from Las Vegas market ranges and marked Market allowance. On each finished job, the office enters what those lines really took (Job file → Allowance check), and Price book offers the job average as the new price. An estimate keeps the prices it was approved or signed with, so later price-book changes never move a price the customer has seen.
  20. Steel is priced only from a hard manufacturer quote. The estimate cannot go for approval, and the proposal stays blocked, until the quote is entered.

In this version, photos are ticked off on a checklist. The live version would attach the photos to each item. Prices are samples.
